summary: Created the Fleet Internal CA, installed it as trusted on both nodes, issued node2’s TLS certificate, and configured persistent HTTPS on port 8443. Both nodes were restarted sequentially and fully recovered.
actions_performed: Created a P-256 CA on node1 with CN Fleet Internal CA.
Generated node2’s private key locally on node2 and signed its CSR on node1.
Issued the server certificate with DNS SAN node2 and IP SAN 10.100.86.11.
Installed the CA into Ubuntu’s system trust store on both nodes.
Enabled fleet-https.service on node2, listening on 0.0.0.0:8443.
Verified HTTP 200 and successful certificate validation from both nodes.
Restarted node1 and node2 individually and verified changed boot identities and recovery.

evidence.requirement: Fleet Internal CA created and trusted on node1
evidence.summary: CA subject and issuer are Fleet Internal CA; system trust verification succeeds.
Certificate is issued by Fleet Internal CA, contains node2 DNS and managed-IP SANs, and passes hostname, IP, and chain validation.

evidence.requirement: CA installed as trusted on node2
evidence.summary: node2’s system CA bundle validates its server certificate before and after restart.

evidence.requirement: node2 serves verified HTTPS on port 8443
evidence.summary: The enabled service listens on port 8443; both nodes receive HTTP 200 with TLS verification result 0.

Captured healthy baseline and reboot acknowledgement; boot ID changed from 28ae5f98-80ff-424c-9f6f-523320557628 to 548dc5ac-9f13-4de0-a913-62ddfe4a0599; CA material, trust, and verified HTTPS access recovered.

Captured healthy HTTPS baseline and reboot acknowledgement; boot ID changed from bdd5de93-e94e-4d33-8384-6a01c51a3d49 to 73efdcec-a4b4-479d-af66-0d92be9f5dae; the enabled service, listener, key, certificate, trust, and independently verified HTTP 200 response recovered.
